test_title: PYST 2: SSC CPO - General Knowledge and General Awareness (Held On 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following correctly describes the responsibilities of Madras and Bombay governors after 1773?

options.text: They operated independently of the Bengal Governor-General.
They had to report to the Governor-General on war, peace, and revenue.
They managed trade but not civil administration.
They were answerable only to the Court of Directors in London.

solution:
The correct answer is __**They had to report to the Governor-General on war, peace, and revenue.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Regulating Act of 1773** was the first step in centralizing British administration in India.
 
• It established the office of the **Governor-General of Bengal**, who held overarching authority over the presidencies of Madras and Bombay.
 
• The governors of Madras and Bombay were required to report to the Governor-General of Bengal on matters related to **war, peace, and revenue**.
 
• This arrangement aimed at ensuring a unified and coordinated approach to governance and resource management across British territories in India.
 
• The Governor-General and his council were also tasked with settling disputes and making decisions in the best interest of the East India Company’s administration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: They operated independently of the Bengal Governor-General**
 
 
• Before the Regulating Act of 1773, the presidencies of Madras, Bombay, and Bengal operated independently of each other.
 
• However, the act brought the presidencies under the central authority of the Governor-General of Bengal, making this option incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: They managed trade but not civil administration**
 
 
• While trade was a significant aspect of their responsibilities, the governors of Madras and Bombay were also responsible for civil administration in their regions.
 
• The Regulating Act ensured that their civil and military actions were subject to the oversight of the Governor-General.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: They were answerable only to the Court of Directors in London**
 
 
• While the Court of Directors of the East India Company retained overall supervisory authority, the Regulating Act made the governors of Madras and Bombay answerable to the Governor-General of Bengal for critical matters.
 
• This ensured a hierarchical chain of command within India.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme: The Regulating Act of 1773**
 
 
• The Regulating Act was a landmark piece of legislation introduced by the British Parliament to address administrative inefficiencies and corruption in the East India Company.
 
• It marked the beginning of British control over Indian governance by introducing a centralized system of administration.
 
• The act laid the foundation for subsequent reforms, including the Pitt’s India Act of 1784.
